# v4.2 Remote paste over SSH

## Summary

- New **remote paste** for CLIs running on a remote host over SSH (#11). When you `ssh` into a server and run Codex / Claude Code / OpenCode there, a local `/mnt/c/...` path is meaningless on the remote side. The hotkey now uploads the clipboard image to the remote host first and pastes the **remote** path instead, so the CLI still renders it as `[Image #n]`
- **Zero configuration.** On each hotkey press the helper enumerates the SSH sessions currently open — Windows-side `ssh.exe` (command line read via `NtQueryInformationProcess`) and `ssh` inside the default WSL distro — and reuses that session's own arguments (user, host, port, `-i`, `-J`, `~/.ssh/config` alias, and the very same `ssh.exe`) for the upload. No session open → local `/mnt` path as before
- Only interactive login sessions count: `ssh -N` tunnels, VS Code Remote-SSH (`-T`), git and other remote-command invocations without `-t` are ignored
- **Only the tab you paste into matters.** With a local tab and an SSH tab side by side in one Windows Terminal window, pressing the hotkey in the local tab still pastes the local path (rendered as `[Image #n]`); only the SSH tab uploads. Tabs are told apart by briefly appending an invisible zero-width character to each tab's console title and watching which one the window title picks up, then restoring it. WSL-side `ssh` is matched to its tab through `WT_SESSION`. When the tab cannot be determined (`suppressApplicationTitle`, non-WT terminals, `ssh` inside tmux/screen) the helper falls back to the newest SSH session of the foreground app
- New tray submenu `远程粘贴（SSH）`: `自动` (default, upload only from an SSH tab), `关闭` (never upload; persisted as `remote_paste = false`), or pin one of the listed sessions to always upload there regardless of the active tab. The tray tooltip shows the current choice
- Transfer uses a single SSH connection (`mkdir -p DIR && cat > DIR/FILE`, file streamed via stdin) into `/tmp/wsl_clipboard-<uid>/` — no `scp`/`sftp-server` needed on the remote
- Files copied in Explorer are uploaded the same way (directories are skipped)
- Re-pasting the same image reuses the already uploaded file; temporary screenshots uploaded during the session are deleted from the remote host on exit, mirroring the local `temp/` cleanup
- Fix re-pasting one image after switching between SSH and local WSL: recognize the helper's own path text using its clipboard sequence and exact content, reuse the original image, and select the destination again. Newly copied text (even the same path) is not treated as the cached image; clipboard changes during upload cancel the stale paste.
- SSH runs with `BatchMode=yes` / `ConnectTimeout=5` and a 60 s overall timeout, so an unreachable host fails fast. Failures are reported through a tray balloon (with a hint about public-key setup) and nothing is pasted
- The helper is a windowless GUI process; `ssh.exe` / `wsl.exe` are launched with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` so no console window flashes
- Single instance: launching `wsl_clipboard.exe` again while it is already running just shows a notice instead of adding a second, hotkey-less tray icon
- Existing `wsl_clipboard.toml` files keep working unchanged; the only new key is the optional `remote_paste` (default `true`)

## Requirement for remote paste

- The remote host must accept **key-based, passwordless** login from the side you `ssh` from (the helper has no console to type a password). If you log in with a password today, add your public key to the remote `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` once per host, e.g. from PowerShell:

  ```powershell
  type $env:USERPROFILE\.ssh\id_ed25519.pub | ssh user@host "mkdir -p ~/.ssh && cat >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys"
  ```
